newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka girds for Tamil rebels' "Heroes Day".
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka girds for Tamil rebels' "Heroes Day".

text.p: Security forces in the Sri Lankan capital of Colombo were on full alert on Wednesday for separatist Tamil Tigers' "National Heroes Day", when the rebels honour fallen fighters, police said.
"We have received all sorts of information that the LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam) will try to create trouble in Colombo," Colombo police chief D.M. Dissanayake said.
"But we have taken precautions to prevent them. We have left no stone unturned," Dissanayake told Reuters.

November 27 is the final day of the LTTE's week-long celebrations to remember fallen fighters, a highlight of which is Tiger leader Velupillai Prabhakaran's birthday. The birthday on Tuesday passed without incident.
The LTTE has traditionally marked heroes' week with attacks on military installations and remote border villages.
The elusive Prabhakaran, 42, is set to address his followers on the LTTE's clandestine "Voice of Tigers" radio on Wednesday evening, the group said.
The army said it was providing maximum round-the-clock security to the capital of the Indian Ocean island nation.
"We were placed on a state of high alert yesterday (for Prabhakaran's birthday). We're not letting off today either," an army spokesman said.
Stepped up security checks caused delays to traffic in much of the capital as cars and passengers were strictly searched.
A statement faxed to Reuters on Wednesday from the LTTE's international secretariat in London said Tamils expressed their heartfelt gratitude and respect for their national heroes.

"Most streets in the Tamil homeland remain brightly decorated with the red and yellow of Tamil Eelam's national flag and the Tamil people are engaged in many cultural activities as well as prayers," the statement said.

Eelam is the Tamil name of the state the LTTE has been waging a 13-year war to create in northern and eastern Sri Lanka for Tamils. Mainly Hindus, Tamils make up 17 percent of a population of predominantly Sinhalese Buddhists.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the conflict. The LTTE says a much larger number have died.
